title: Retrieval Augmented Generation in the Wild: Anton Troynikov
talk_summary: Anton Troynikov argues basic top-k RAG is an open loop; production agents need retrieval that filters irrelevant context, supports feedback/self-updates, and is evaluated on your own data. He details practical levers: relevance feedback, reranking/conditional relevance, structure-aware chunking, and testing embedding/chunking choices against production-derived datasets.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of always returning top-k, use a reranker or conditional relevance signal to decide whether retrieved results are relevant; if none are relevant, return none.
takeaways.evidence_quote: distractors in the model context cause the performance of the entire AI based application to fall off a cliff

takeaways.what_they_do: Use open-source benchmark tooling on your own data and use cases, because academic retrieval benchmarks are saturated and may not reflect production AI use.
takeaways.evidence_quote: take some of the open source tooling built to build these benchmarks in the first place and apply it to your data sets

takeaways.what_they_do: Make the retrieval/memory layer support self-updates from the agent itself, so interactions can update the searchable dataset rather than relying on a static index.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your retrieval system your memory needs to support uh self updates from the agent itself out of the box

takeaways.what_they_do: Add a simple endpoint/UI for humans to mark retrieved results as relevant or irrelevant, creating labels for retrieval evaluation and adaptation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use human feedback on relevance by adding a simple relevance feedback endpoint

takeaways.what_they_do: Respect the natural structure of data because human-readable text/code contains cues about semantic boundaries; chunk along those boundaries rather than fixed windows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: respecting the natural structure of the data because often especially textual data was generated for humans to read and understand

takeaways.what_they_do: Generate a conditional relevancy signal per user, task, model, and task instance using a lightweight model that understands query semantics and dataset content.
takeaways.evidence_quote: generate a conditional relevancy signal per user per task per model and per instance of that task
